newsitem.title: BRAZIL: No coffee frosts reported so far - Brazil growers.
newsitem.headline: No coffee frosts reported so far - Brazil growers.

text.p: Brazilian cooperative officials and growers in the country's coldest coffee regions had not heard of any frosts on coffee farms by 1030 GMT on Monday morning.

"There have been frosts in low-lying areas where there is no coffee. But I have not heard of any frosts in coffee farms," said Gilson Ximenes, president of the growers' National Coffee Council and of the cooperative in Tres Pontas, Minas Gerais state.

Jose Geraldo Rodrigues, superintendent at the cooperative in Guaxupe where temperatures fell to three degrees Celsius this morning, said that any frosts were thought to occurred only at lower altitudes and that there had been no reports so far of damage to coffee.
In many coffee regions in Brazil, the lowest temperatures are seen in low-lying areas and not on the slopes where the crop is grown.
Current low temperatures are due to a polar air mass that has entered the country over land and is expected to keep conditions cold through to Wednesday.
Local forecasters have alerted growers to the possibility of frosts in low-lying areas but damage to the coffee crop is seen unlikely.
